facts.statement: The genus Curvorudentis is considered a valid taxon.
Curvorudentis belongs to the subclass Galeomorphii of uncertain affinities.
facts.quote: A member of Galeomorphii of uncertain affinities.

facts.statement: The type species of Curvorudentis is the former Synechodus prorogatus described by Kriwet in 2003.
facts.quote: The type species is "Synechodus" prorogatus Kriwet (2003).

facts.statement: Curvorudentis is placed in the class Chondrichthyes.
Fossil occurrences of Curvorudentis have been recorded from four localities.
Curvorudentis lived during the Callovian to Kimmeridgian ages of the Middle to Late Jurassic, about 165.3 to 152.21 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Kimmeridgian (165.3 to 152.21 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Curvorudentis have been found in Germany and Poland.
The original description of Synechodus prorogatus was based on a single complete tooth and two very incomplete teeth.
New material from Upper Jurassic offshore deposits in southwestern Germany provided additional information leading to the erection of the new genus Curvorudentis.
The discovery of Curvorudentis in Late Jurassic deposits of Germany extends its chronostratigraphic range to the youngest Jurassic occurrence.
Curvorudentis prorogatus is interpreted as a galeomorph shark rather than a member of the stem clade Synechodontiformes.
The precise systematic position of Curvorudentis within Galeomorphii remains ambiguous.

rejected.statement: Curvorudentis is a newly established genus and combination described in 2026 by Begat and colleagues.
The revision establishing Curvorudentis was published in the Swiss Journal of Palaeontology in 2026 by Begat, Villalobos‑Segura, Amadori, Klug, and Kriwet.
